Generated Reference

Generated from cli-contract.json

CLI リファレンス

これは権威あるネイティブ CLI 契約 rust/fslc/cli-contract.json から生成されています。各コマンドの使い方はネイティブ fslc の --help 出力そのものです。src/fslc/ の凍結 Python 互換参照は配布面ではなく、明示的な parity テスト用のみに言及します。

Exit codes & JSON envelope — docs/LANGUAGE.md + rust/fslc/src/outcome.rs::exit_status()

The authoritative native CLI maps every JSON result to a process exit code through rust/fslc/src/outcome.rs exit_status(), which implements the table in docs/LANGUAGE.md:

Exit codes: `0` = verified / proved / scenarios/testgen generated / conformant / refines /
mutated / explained / analyzed / semantic_diff (unless its explicit gate fails) /
typestate / sweep_passed / observed_conformant /
imported / imported_with_warnings,
`1` = violated / reachable_failed / unknown_cti / unknown_budget / nonconformant /
refinement_failed / sweep_failed / observed_mismatch,
`2` = spec error (parse / type / semantics / io / vacuous / acceptance / forbidden /
`--vacuity error`), `3` = internal error. `observed_*` is `fslc db observe`'s
result; `imported`/`imported_with_warnings` is `fslc db import`'s. The same
`2` mapping is fail-closed for `chain`'s project-manifest reader (unrecognized
section, zero recognized sections, or an unparseable `depth`/`refine_depth` —
`docs/DESIGN-layers.md` §7) and for `ledger --impl-log`'s replay input (a
replay error is not implementation-log evidence and must not be rendered as
an empty ledger row — `docs/DESIGN-ledger.md`).

Verdict-bearing commands print one JSON object to stdout with {"fsl":"1.0", ...}, and the exit code is derived from its result. Commands that emit a generated artifact write that artifact to stdout under some flag combinations instead — fslc fmt PATH prints formatted source, while fslc fmt --check returns a format_check envelope, and document, db, and domain subcommands print generated content or return an envelope depending on whether an output path is given. The rule is per command and per flag, so read a command's own --help before parsing its stdout as JSON. Native CLI and browser Worker check/verify envelopes also include versions.verifier, versions.core, and versions.solver (see docs/LANGUAGE.md §14). The machine-readable schema is schemas/fslc/envelope.v1.schema.json. The frozen Python compatibility reference under src/fslc/ mirrors a subset for parity tests only — it is not the distribution surface.

usage: fslc document generate [-h] [--view {requirements}] [--lang {ja,en}] [--strict] [--strict-rendering] [--glossary GLOSSARY] [--evidence EVIDENCE] [--approval RECORD] [--trust-key PUBLIC_KEY] [-o OUTPUT] file

positional arguments:
  file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --view {requirements}
                        v1 supports only requirements; reserved for
                        business/design (#334)
  --lang {ja,en}        controlled-language locale (default: ja)
  --strict              fail if an authored target is unattributed or
                        unsupported (FSL-DOC-UNTAGGED-TARGET /
                        FSL-DOC-UNSUPPORTED-TARGET), or a glossary target
                        does not exist (FSL-DOC-LABEL-UNKNOWN)
  --strict-rendering    fail if an expression falls back to canonical FSL
                        text (FSL-DOC-FORMULA-FALLBACK)
  --glossary GLOSSARY   presentation-only display-label sidecar
                        (fslc.document-glossary.v1); a duplicate target is
                        always an error (FSL-DOC-LABEL-CONFLICT)
  --evidence EVIDENCE   saved evidence envelope (JSON, same shape as 'fslc
                        ledger --evidence') overlaid onto the document as a
                        per-requirement assurance class
                        (proved/bounded/replay-observed/statistical); does
                        not run any verification itself; repeatable; an
                        unmatched file is a warning by default, an error
                        under --strict (FSL-DOC-EVIDENCE-UNMATCHED)
  --approval RECORD     a requirements_document approval record (from 'fslc
                        approval create --kind requirements_document') to
                        display as an "Approval records" section; repeatable;
                        must match the current rendering exactly or this
                        fails closed (FSL-DOC-APPROVAL-DRIFTED); a signed
                        record requires a matching --trust-key
                        (FSL-DOC-APPROVAL-INVALID otherwise)
  --trust-key PUBLIC_KEY
                        trusted SPKI Ed25519 public key for a signed
                        --approval record; repeatable
  -o, --output OUTPUT

fslc document check
usage: fslc document check [-h] [--glossary GLOSSARY] [--evidence EVIDENCE] [--approval RECORD] file document

positional arguments:
  file      the FSL spec the document was generated from
  document  the generated Markdown artifact (from 'fslc document generate')

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --glossary GLOSSARY   the same glossary sidecar 'generate' was given, if
                        any; a mismatch (missing, extra, or different
                        content) is reported as glossary_changed
                        (FSL-DOC-GLOSSARY-CHANGED), not a hard error
  --evidence EVIDENCE   the same evidence files 'generate' was given, if
                        any; a mismatch is reported as evidence_changed
                        (FSL-DOC-EVIDENCE-CHANGED), not a hard error;
                        repeatable
  --approval RECORD     the same approval record(s) 'generate' was given, if
                        any; a mismatch is reported as approval_changed
                        (FSL-DOC-APPROVAL-CHANGED), not a hard error;
                        repeatable; never verifies a signature (admission
                        is 'generate's job, this only reproduces display text)

Structural drift check only: no natural language is interpreted. Reads the
locale and source label back from the artifact's own frontmatter, re-projects
and re-renders the spec, and compares claim/slot marker structure and
claim-block digests. Exit codes: 0 document_conformant, 1 document_drifted,
2 parse/type/semantics/schema/I/O error, 3 internal error.

usage: fslc verify [-h] [--depth DEPTH] [--engine {bmc,induction,explicit,auto}] [--k K_IND] [--explicit-budget EXPLICIT_BUDGET] [--deadlock {warn,error,ignore}] [--vacuity {warn,error,ignore}] [--property PROPERTY_NAME] [--exclude-property EXCLUDE_PROPERTY_NAMES] [--instances INSTANCES] [--values VALUES] [--strict-tags] [--requirements REQUIREMENTS] [--no-cache] [--lemma LEMMAS] [--from-state FROM_STATE] [--edition {current,next}] file

positional arguments:
  file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --depth DEPTH
  --engine {bmc,induction,explicit,auto}
  --k K_IND             max induction depth (induction engine only)
  --explicit-budget EXPLICIT_BUDGET
                        max visited states for the explicit engine (default
                        1000000); exceeding returns unknown_budget
  --deadlock {warn,error,ignore}
  --vacuity {warn,error,ignore}
  --property PROPERTY_NAME
                        select one named property obligation; resolves across
                        invariant/trans/leadsTo/reachable declarations; under
                        induction, a selected trans keeps all invariant
                        hypotheses
  --exclude-property EXCLUDE_PROPERTY_NAMES
                        skip a named property; repeat to omit
                        invariants/trans/leadsTo/reachable declarations
  --instances INSTANCES
                        override a verify-block 'instances NAME = N' bound
                        (NAME=N; repeatable) — e.g. shrink to 1 entity for
                        liveness
  --values VALUES       override a verify-block 'values NAME = LO..HI' bound
                        (NAME=LO..HI; repeatable)
  --strict-tags
  --requirements REQUIREMENTS
  --no-cache            skip the persistent verdict cache for this run (neither
                        reads nor writes it)
  --lemma LEMMAS        candidate auxiliary invariant expression (induction
                        only; repeatable)
  --from-state FROM_STATE
                        replace spec init with a complete Monitor/replay
                        logical-state JSON snapshot (BMC only)
  --edition {current,next}
fslc conformance
usage: fslc conformance [-h] [--depth DEPTH] [--kernel-version {1,2}] file

positional arguments:
  file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --depth DEPTH         maximum transition depth (default: 4)
  --kernel-version {1,2}
                        public Kernel major (default: 1)
fslc testplan
usage: fslc testplan [-h] [--depth DEPTH] file

Select bounded conformance vectors into a closed test-plan.v1 JSON plan.
Pass the spec at the same FSL layer granularity as the implementation you are checking; from an upper layer reuse forbidden (negative) scenarios only.

positional arguments:
  file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --depth DEPTH         maximum transition depth (default: 4)
fslc counterexample — 1 subcommands
usage: fslc counterexample [-h] {export}

positional arguments:
  {export}            export a bounded safety-invariant counterexample to reproducer.v1

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
fslc counterexample export
usage: fslc counterexample export [-h] [--depth DEPTH] [--engine {bmc,explicit,auto,induction}] [--deadlock {warn,error,ignore}] -o OUTPUT file

Export a bounded safety-invariant counterexample as a closed reproducer.v1 JSON artifact.

positional arguments:
  file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --depth DEPTH         maximum transition depth (default: 8)
  --engine {bmc,explicit,auto,induction}
                        verification engine (default: bmc)
  --deadlock {warn,error,ignore}
                        deadlock reporting policy (default: warn)
  -o OUTPUT, --output OUTPUT
                        reproducer artifact output path (required)
fslc kernel
usage: fslc kernel [-h] [--kernel-version {1,2}] file

positional arguments:
  file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --kernel-version {1,2}
                        public Kernel major (default: 1)
fslc fmt
usage: fslc fmt [-h] [--check] [--edition {current,next}] path [path ...]

Format one registered FSL document to stdout without mutating it. Multiple paths are accepted only with --check. Use '-' for stdin.

positional arguments:
  path

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --check               report whether formatting is required (exit 0 clean, 1 changed)
  --edition {current,next}
                        formatting policy (default: current)
fslc lint
usage: fslc lint [-h] [--edition {current,next}] [--project PROJECT] path [path ...]

Report stable edition and ID-policy diagnostics without mutating source files.

positional arguments:
  path

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --edition {current,next}
                        lint policy (default: current)
  --project PROJECT     explicit fsl-project.toml ID-policy manifest
fslc migrate
usage: fslc migrate [-h] [--edition {current,next}] [--write] path [path ...]

Plan machine-applicable edition edits without mutation. --write applies the validated file set atomically.

positional arguments:
  path

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --edition {current,next}
                        target edition (default: next)
  --write               atomically replace every validated input file
